recent_articles.title: Families urged to consider fortified rice to improve nutrient supply - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Dinesh Gundu Rao**, **India’s Health and Family Welfare Minister**, urged families to consume fortified rice to ensure adequate nutrition.  He noted the rising prevalence of lifestyle diseases like diabetes and hypertension, emphasizing the importance of including beneficial nutrients in staples like rice.  **Usharani Dandamundi**, a food scientist from the CSIR-CFTRI, highlighted the issue of nutrient insecurity in India, with 60% of Indians facing "hidden hunger." She emphasized that polished white rice can lead to deficiencies in essential nutrients. **Panchamrutha Industries’ managing director, Jumbulingappa Hosmani**, stated that fortified rice is a transformative tool for improving public health outcomes and highlighted the growing interest in fortified rice across India.  **Millers for Nutrition**, an industry-led coalition focused on combatting malnutrition through food fortification, supports scaling up fortified staples like rice to advance nutrition security.

recent_articles.title: Govt. plans security protocol for fishing harbours under CISF oversight - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Central Industrial Security Force (CISF)** will oversee the security of around 1,200 fishing harbours and landing sites across India as part of a plan to strengthen the country's coastline. The **Union Home Ministry** aims to implement this framework after assigning CISF personnel to secure 250 seaports. This move follows guidelines issued by the **Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA)** in 2023, and is intended to provide a uniform security template for all coastal areas.  The government's objective is to ensure the safety of fisherfolk and prevent potential threats like those seen during the 26/11 Mumbai attacks.

recent_articles.title: Congress asks its rank and file to be alert against deletion of voters ahead of SIR exercise in Karnataka - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Congress** leaders are concerned about the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise in Karnataka, fearing voter suppression similar to what happened in West Bengal. The party has urged its rank and file to remain vigilant and is preparing for potential challenges. **Randeep Surjewala**, Congress general secretary in charge of Karnataka, emphasized the importance of educating voters about SIR's implications.  The State government is expected to respond to the concerns raised by the party soon.

recent_articles.title: Kasaragod district administration prepares railway master plan to end travel hardships - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Kasaragod** district administration has proposed a comprehensive railway master plan to address travel hardships faced by passengers in the northern Kerala region. The proposals, submitted to **Palakkad Divisional Railway Manager (DRM) Madhukar Rawat**, include extending eight trains currently terminating at Kannur and Mangaluru Central/Junction to Kasaragod, as well as restoring discontinued passenger services. The administration also seeks stoppages for three major superfast trains that currently bypass Kasaragod station. These proposals aim to benefit passengers travelling for work, education, medical treatment, pilgrimage, and trade.  The district administration has requested the railway authorities to consider these proposals for improved convenience and efficient travel for residents of Kasaragod.

recent_articles.title: 68% of flyover on Anna Salai completed despite delays due to war, labour shortage - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **State Highways Department** officials report that nearly 68% of the construction project for a flyover on Anna Salai, connecting Saidapet and Teynampet, has been completed.  The project is expected to be finished by September with 32 out of 131 decks in place. The completion of the flyover will involve placing slabs on girders, completing foundation work for pillars, and installing approach ramps and crash barriers.

recent_articles.title: NEET paper leak row: Congress demands resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Congress** leaders demanded the resignation of **Dharmendra Pradhan**, the **Union Education Minister**, over the NEET-UG paper leak scandal.  They accused the government of a "money-making racket" involving people linked to the ruling establishment and claimed that the incident had caused immense trauma for 22 lakh students. **Rahul Gandhi** called for the Prime Minister's intervention, while **Mallikarjun Kharge**, the Congress president, alleged that the Modi government was undermining student credibility through repeated paper leaks.  **Jairam Ramesh**, a Congress general secretary, criticized the government's lack of action and incompetence in addressing exam reforms.

recent_articles.title: Supreme Court closes plea of Goa Congress leader after his death from snakebite - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Supreme Court** closed the plea of deceased **Ketan Bhatikar**, a Congress candidate for the Ponda Assembly seat, challenging a Bombay High Court order cancelling the bypoll.  Bhatikar died from a snakebite on Thursday and his lawyer requested the court to leave the larger question of law open while closing the proceedings. The High Court had earlier canceled the bypoll citing violation of the Representation of the People Act as less than one year remained in the term of the Assembly.

recent_articles.title: Sebi approves IPO plans of Neolite Lightings, Aspri Spirits and SS Retail - The Economic Times
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Neolite ZKW Lightings**, a manufacturer of automotive lighting products, plans to raise Rs 600 crore through a combination of fresh issue and offer-for-sale. The IPO will be used for setting up a greenfield manufacturing facility in Kancheepuram, Tamil Nadu, expanding existing operations, and repaying borrowings. **Neolite ZKW Lightings** has a significant market share in India's commercial vehicle lighting segment and serves over 40 OEM customers. Meanwhile, **Aspri Spirits**, an importer and distributor of international wine and spirits, received Sebi approval for its public issue with a proposed IPO of up to Rs 140 crore.  SS Retail, another company seeking regulatory clearance, plans to raise Rs 500 crore through its IPO, which will be used for expansion and growth.

recent_articles.title: ECI set to roll out phase III of SIR in ‘coming days’ to cover 22 States, UTs - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Election Commission of India (ECI)** is set to begin phase three of its Special Intensive Revision (SIR) voter list process in the coming days, covering nearly 40 crore electors across 17 states and five UTs.  This follows completion of SIR in 10 states and three UTs previously, which has successfully removed over 60 lakh deceased voters from the rolls. The ECI had initially delayed the rollout due to Assembly elections in several states but is now proceeding with the revision process.  The exercise aims to ensure accurate voter lists for upcoming elections.

recent_articles.title: Governor’s role in government formation | Explained - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK)** secured a majority in the recent Tamil Nadu Assembly elections, but the Governor invited the party's chief to form the government.  **C. Joseph Vijay**, the TVK leader, was sworn in as Chief Minister after securing letters of support from 120 members. The Governor's discretion in appointing the Chief Minister is based on constitutional provisions and previous recommendations by commissions, but there have been instances where Governors have appointed a Chief Minister without following these guidelines.  The Supreme Court has emphasized that the "floor of the House" is the appropriate forum to determine majority support for a government.

recent_articles.title: PM Modi assures more support to Telangana, asks CM Revanth to collaborate with him - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** assured **Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy** that the **Central government** would continue to support its development, emphasizing the importance of state-level progress for a developed India by 2047.  During his visit on May 10, 2026, **Modi** inaugurated several developmental projects worth ₹9,400 crore, including industrial parks and railway infrastructure, aiming to make Telangana a manufacturing hub. He highlighted the government's commitment to creating employment opportunities and reviving the textile industry through schemes like PM Mitra Park at Warangal and investments in infrastructure development.  The Prime Minister also emphasized the importance of energy security with the launch of the Malkapur terminal.

recent_articles.title: Census enumerators ID can be verified through QR code - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Lalit Jain**, Director of Census Operations (DCO), **Haryana**, has introduced QR code-enabled identity cards for enumerators to address concerns about authenticity.  Jain explained that residents can verify the legitimacy of enumerators by scanning the codes on their ID cards. The first phase of the digital census, which began on April 1, aims to cover over 30 lakh households across India. Residents are legally obligated to answer Census-related questions, and while there have been no cases of FIRs for non-response, local authorities will be involved in encouraging participation.  The second phase of the census, focusing on caste enumeration, is scheduled for February 2027.

recent_articles.title: Gurugram gated societies not letting in enumerators; FIRs recommended against enumerators obstructing Census work - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Haryana** administration has recommended an FIR against two government school staff for alleged negligence in Census-related work and obstruction of duties.  **Gurugram Municipal Corporation Joint Commissioner Punit Kumar** stated that enumerators have been denied entry into several highrise apartment buildings, prompting him to write to RWAs to ensure their access. **Registrar General of India Mritunjay Kumar Narayan** flagged off awareness vans across Delhi for the ongoing Census 2027 public outreach campaign.  The first phase of the Census began on April 1 and will conclude by September 30, involving around 30 lakh enumerators.

recent_articles.title: Urrak: Goa’s liquid summer soul - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Goans** have a deep connection to the cashew tree, which is integral to their culture and agriculture. The tree's adaptability to infertile soil and its strong roots make it ideal for coastal planting, providing protection for farmlands in the interior.  The fruit is fermented into **urrak**, an alcoholic beverage that is considered a symbol of Goa's traditional spirit and a key element of summer celebrations.  **Urrak** production relies on ancient techniques like foot-crushing to extract juice, emphasizing sustainability and community involvement. The unique flavor profile of **urrak** makes it distinct from mass-produced spirits and is enjoyed by locals in their homes, often accompanied by local cuisine.

recent_articles.title: Urrak: How the jungle juice from Goa is having its moment - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Urrak**, a cashew-based spirit, has experienced a surge in popularity in Goa, becoming the state's official summer drink.  Its accessibility and refreshing taste have contributed to its widespread appeal, with **Mac Vaz**, founder of the All Goa Cashew Feni Distillers & Bottlers Association, noting that it is "deceptively smooth" and hangover-free. The spirit has also garnered attention from mixologists who are experimenting with new cocktails featuring urrak, further boosting its popularity.  **Deviya Rane**, MLA and chairperson of the Goa Forest Development Corporation, recognizes the cultural significance of urrak and supports efforts to elevate it to a premium status globally through initiatives like the Cashew Fest.

recent_articles.title: Census 2027: Around 82 lakh households have opted for self enumeration as field visits begin in 5 states - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Union government** announced that over 82 lakh households have utilized the self-enumeration facility during the initial Houselisting and Housing Operations (HLO) phase of Census 2027. The exercise, which commenced on May 1st in several states including Andhra Pradesh, Haryana, Chandigarh, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, and Rajasthan, aims to collect data about household facilities and demographics.  The HLO will continue until May 30th, with trained enumerators visiting each house for verification.

recent_articles.title: Two highway defects in Karnataka over three years: Debarment, repairs ordered - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **National Highways (NHs)** in Karnataka have experienced two major incidents of structural defects and collapses over the past three years.  In 2025, a reinforced earth wall block collapsed on NH-948, prompting repair work based on recommendations from **Indian Institute of Science (IISc)** experts. In 2024, the Kali Bridge on NH-66 collapsed due to inadequate slope stability works, leading to the contractor's one-month debarment and corrective measures.  The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has taken action against defaulting agencies based on severity of violations, including penalties, contract termination, or blacklisting.

recent_articles.title: Meta sets up automatic blocking for govt., police-referred content - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Meta**, the parent company of **Facebook** and **Instagram**, has been complying with censorship orders from Indian authorities, restricting content on its platforms based on local laws. The Sahyog portal, used by police to request takedowns, allows for immediate restriction of access without requiring a formal legal process.  The firm's response is to instantly remove content flagged through this mechanism, even after determining the takedown may be legally improper. Critics argue that this practice creates an "infrastructure of censorship" and undermines free speech, while experts call on **Meta** to publish all takedown notices and challenge frivolous ones in court.

recent_articles.title: Earth Day 2026: How Nature walks, parks, and trails are sparking a new conservation movement - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rohit Girotra**, co-founder of the Bangalore Butterfly Club (BBC), has seen a surge in interest in butterflies and butterfly-focused activities. The BBC, which began in 2012, now boasts nearly 600 members and offers guided walks at Doresanipalya Forest Research Station.  **Ashok Sengupta**, another BBC co-founder, believes that butterfly watching is an easy portal into the natural world for children. **Isaac Kehimkar**, a naturalist and photographer, has documented over 40 Facebook groups dedicated to butterflies worldwide. These groups have helped raise awareness of these insects through social media and mobile cameras. Butterfly parks and trails are also becoming increasingly popular across India, with locations like Sammilan Shetty's Butterfly Park in Karnataka offering educational programs on butterfly conservation.

recent_articles.title: Govt claims women winning unreserved panchayat seats in ‘significant numbers’ - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Union Government** celebrated National Panchayati Raj Day, highlighting the progress of women's reservation in Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs).  While the Constitution mandates a 33% quota for women in urban and rural local bodies, 19 states have extended this provision to reserve 50% seats for women. However, data shows that the actual number of women representatives exceeds the prescribed quota in only 10 states/union territories, while four others fail to meet it.  The Ministry emphasized the increasing representation of women in PRIs, but acknowledged discrepancies between mandated and achieved quotas across various states.

recent_articles.title: Pakistan out of women’s football tournament in India over political strife | Football News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Pakistan**'s women's football team will not participate in the **South Asian Football Federation (SAFF)** Women’s Championship hosted in India due to ongoing geopolitical tensions between the two nations. The Pakistani government has barred the team from traveling, citing a lack of an NOC from relevant authorities.  The tournament is scheduled for May 25 to June 7 and will be held at Goa's Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium. This decision follows a long history of strained relations between India and **Pakistan**, which have impacted cross-border travel for athletes in various sports, including cricket.

recent_articles.title: SIR is a bloodless massacre, says Parakala Prabhakar - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Parakala Prabhakar**, a political and economic analyst, criticized the proposed **Special Integrated Revision (SIR)** of electoral rolls in Telangana, calling it a "bloodless massacre" that threatens democratic rights. He questioned the need for a fresh revision when the annual Special Summary Revision (SSR) is already in place, criticizing the **Election Commission of India**'s justification and lack of transparency regarding irregularities and data released. Prabhakar cited examples from other states where SIR resulted in voter deletions with unclear criteria and inconsistencies, urging the government to first prepare the voter list through the State Election Commission before implementing SIR.

recent_articles.title: Indian heritage spirits Mahua and Goan Feni debut in UK market | World News - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Mahua** and **Feni**, traditional Indian spirits, have entered the UK market through **Maharaja Drinks**. The retailer launched a new range featuring three Feni variants and one **Mahua** spirit, made using small-batch distillation methods and natural ingredients.  The move aims to bring authentic native flavors to a wider audience while appealing to the Indian diaspora in the UK.

recent_articles.title: Door-to-door visit by Census enumerators in eight States/U.T.s from April 16 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA)** announced the commencement of door-to-door enumeration for the first phase of the 2027 Population Census, known as the House Listing and Housing Operations (HLO). Beginning on April 16th in eight states and union territories including Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Goa, Karnataka, Lakshadweep, Mizoram, Odisha, Sikkim, and Delhi's NDMC area and Cantonment Board, enumerators will collect data for the HLO phase. This follows a 15-day self-enumeration period.

recent_articles.title: Consolidated voters’ list of 9 States and 3 UTs that underwent SIR Phase II trimmed by 10.2% - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Election Commission of India** announced the results of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in nine states and three Union Territories. **Uttar Pradesh** recorded the highest net deletion of voters at 2.04 crore, followed by **West Bengal**, with a net deletion of 83.86 lakh. The SIR phase II identified 67 lakh deceased voters and 1.28 crore duplicate voters across these states and UTs.  The consolidated electoral rolls saw a reduction of 10.2%, bringing the number of active voters down to 45.81 crore.

recent_articles.title: Consolidated voters’ list of 12 States and UTs that underwent SIR Phase II trimmed by 10.2% - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Election Commission of India** announced the results of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, which saw a significant reduction in voter numbers across nine states and three Union Territories. **Uttar Pradesh** recorded the highest net deletion of voters at 2.04 crore, followed by West Bengal with 83.86 lakh.  The revision identified 67 lakh deceased voters and 1.28 crore duplicate voters for removal. The consolidated electoral rolls across these regions saw a reduction of 10.2%, bringing the number of active voters down to 45.81 crore.

recent_articles.title: Census 2027: Self-enumeration facility availed by 5.72 lakh households so far in first phase - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Registrar General of India (RGI)** announced that over 5.72 lakh households have utilized the self-enumeration facility during the first phase of the Census 2027. This digital initiative reflects growing participation in the census, with a special portal available for citizens in specific areas including Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Goa, Karnataka, Sikkim, Odisha, Lakshadweep, Mizoram, and Delhi's NDMC and Cantonment Board. The self-enumeration facility allows citizens to provide their details online, facilitating a faster and more convenient contribution to nation-building.

recent_articles.title: Assembly elections 2026 LIVE updates: Voting begins in a single phase today in Assam, Kerala and Puducherry - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Kerala**, **Assam**, and **Puducherry** held single-phase elections on April 9, 2026, with voting concluding at 5 p.m.  The results will be announced on May 4. The high-stakes elections in **Assam** are expected to see the BJP vying for a third consecutive term. In **Kerala**, three fronts – the CPI(M)-led LDF, the Congress-led UDF and the BJP-led NDA – are contesting across 140 constituencies.  The bypolls also took place in several states including Gujarat, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Nagaland and Tripura.

recent_articles.title: BJP, the known unknown in Kerala 2026 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The BJP's emergence in Kerala has significantly altered the political landscape, with traditional rivals, the Congress-led UDF and CPI-M-led LDF, aligning their campaigns against each other. The BJP claims a false fight between the two parties while emphasizing its stance on the Sabarimala issue.  While the BJP seeks to capitalize on Hindu sentiment in Kerala, the UDF faces challenges from internal divisions within its Christian and Muslim communities.  The LDF has abandoned its previous stance on women's entry into the Sabarimala shrine, aligning with the BJP's position. The outcome of these elections remains uncertain due to a complex interplay of religious affiliations, demographic shifts, and political maneuvering.

recent_articles.title: Bombay HC quashes ECI notification for Goa’s Ponda bye-election, day before polling - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Bombay High Court** has canceled the scheduled April 9th Ponda Assembly bye-election, ruling that a by-election is not required due to the remaining term of the Goa Legislative Assembly being less than one year. The court's decision was based on petitions filed by two voters who argued against the necessity of holding the election under the Representation of the People Act. **Congress** leader and Central Working Committee member Girish Chodankar has announced plans to appeal the High Court's ruling to the Supreme Court, alleging that the ruling BJP colluded with the Election Commission to cancel the poll.

recent_articles.title: Time to bring youth back to sports from drugs: CM Revanth Reddy - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy** expressed concern over youth disengagement from sports, emphasizing the need to redirect them towards constructive activities like football.  He presented the winning trophy to the **CISF team** at the 74th B.N. Mullik Memorial All India Police Football Championship held in Gachibowli Indoor Stadium.  The tournament saw participation from teams across the country, with the **CISF** men's team claiming victory and **Assam Rifles** winning the women's category. The event was attended by senior officials including **Cyberabad Commissioner M. Ramesh**, **Director General of Police B. Shivadhar Reddy**, and **Telangana Sports Minister Vakiti Srihari**.

recent_articles.title: PM’s push for increasing seats of Lok Sabha, assemblies nothing but ‘Weapon of Mass Distraction’: Congress - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Congress** party criticized Prime Minister Narendra Modi's proposal to increase the number of Lok Sabha seats, accusing him of "hoodwinking" the public and using it as a distraction from other issues. The party argues that the proposal would disproportionately benefit larger states while diminishing the influence of smaller ones.  They also expressed concern about the government's attempt to implement the women's reservation law before the delimitation exercise is complete, arguing that this could have negative consequences for certain states. **Jairam Ramesh**, a Congress general secretary, called the proposal a "Weapon of Mass Distraction (WMD)" and urged the government to prioritize meaningful consultations and public debate.

recent_articles.title: States that stabilised population will not lose Lok Sabha seats: Modi - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** addressed concerns about the impact of population control on Lok Sabha seat allocation, stating that **States** with stabilized populations will not lose their seats. The government plans to amend the Constitution and relevant laws to redraw the electoral map ahead of the 2029 general election, increasing the size of both the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies by half, with a third reserved for women.  Parliament's budget session is reconvening on April 16th to consider these amendments.

recent_articles.title: Census 2027 kicks off: How to do self-enumeration: step-by-step guide - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **India's** Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner will conduct the 2027 census, a massive administrative and statistical exercise that collects demographic data on the entire country. The self-enumeration facility allows citizens to provide their household information online before enumerators visit, offering flexibility in filling out the census schedule.  The dates for self-enumeration vary by state and union territory, with most starting in April 2026. Census data is expected to be published within 2027 due to the digital nature of the process.

recent_articles.title: 55,000 households use Census self-enumeration portal on day one - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **President Droupadi Murmu**, **Vice-President C.P. Radhakrishnan**, **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**, and **Union Home Minister Amit Shah** were among the first to use the online self-enumeration portal for the 2027 Population Census in eight States and Union Territories. The portal, which launched on April 1, 2026, allows households to provide information about their housing conditions and assets before enumerators visit.  The first phase of the census, focusing on house listing operations and housing census (HLO), will run until May 15th in these areas. Data collected through self-enumeration is confidential and will be used for evidence-based planning and policy formulation.

recent_articles.title: Census 2027: India begins counting a billion-plus people in mega exercise
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **India** is launching its largest census in over 15 years, with a goal of capturing demographic and socioeconomic data on its more than 1.4 billion people. The two-phase exercise will involve over three million officials collecting information on housing conditions, household assets, education, migration, and fertility.  The census will also include caste data, marking a significant shift in focus from basic demographics to broader socio-economic indicators. This comprehensive data collection is crucial for policymaking, welfare delivery, and political representation as India's population continues to evolve.

recent_articles.title: India’s untapped ocean ingredient: The rise of native seaweed - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: In Sindhudurg, **India**, a growing movement is bringing seaweed from the intertidal zone to the plates of chefs and consumers.  **The Good Ocean**, founded by **Gabriella D’Cruz**, works with local harvesters to supply food-grade Indian seaweed, including sargassum, to restaurants like **Coco Shambhala**. The organization ensures sustainable harvesting practices and provides a higher income for local workers compared to traditional methods. Chefs are incorporating seaweed into dishes, recognizing its unique flavor profile and potential as a culinary ingredient.  This shift reflects a growing awareness of the ocean's bounty and its role in modern cuisine.

recent_articles.title: Press Club of India issues election reporting advisory to media - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Press Council of India (PCI)** has issued guidelines for media outlets covering the upcoming elections in Assam, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, West Bengal, and Puducherry. The council advised against "paid news" and urged adherence to journalistic conduct regarding pre-poll and exit polls.  It also cautioned against reporting that promotes enmity or hatred between groups based on religion, race, caste, etc., and emphasized the prohibition of publishing false statements about candidates' personal character.

recent_articles.title: Belagavi Police arrest two for online job scam - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Belagavi Police** arrested two individuals, Megha Maradolkar and Hyderali Ghulamali Ujjainwala, for running an online fraud scheme that promised "Work From Home" opportunities and government loan assistance. The suspects used personal documentation to open bank accounts in the names of unsuspecting citizens, which they then used to transfer stolen funds.  **Police Commissioner** Borase Bhushan Gulabarao commended officers involved in the investigation, urging citizens to be cautious about sharing personal information online.
